Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

FOOTBALLS, VOLLEYBALLS, BASKETBALLS, 

NETBALLS, THROWBALLS, AND WATER-POLO BALLS 

PARTV THROWBALLS 

( Third Revision ) 
(Incorporating Amendment No. 1) 



CQ 



£ 



1 



Q 



1. Scope — Covers dimensional and other requirements for throwballs excluding the bladder. 

2. Shape and Dimensions 

2.1 When fully inflated the ball shall be spherical in shape with circumference of 68 to 73.7 cm. 
Fig. 1 deleted 

2.1.1 A tolerance of 1 percent in the circumference on sphericity shall be allowed. 

2.2 Mass of the ball with fully inflated bladder shall be 397 to 454 g. 

2.3 Colour — The colour of the balls shall be subject to requirements of the purchaser. 

3. Materials for Construction 

3.1 Leather — The balls shall be manufactured from butt portion of tight-textured cowhide or 
buffalohide, free from flay cuts and grain defects, vegetable/semi-chrome or chrome tanned, dyed in 
any colour or pigmented as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. At the end of tanning 
operation, and before drying, suitable fungicides shall be incorporated into the leather for promoting 
resistance to mould growth in the leather, these shall be effective and non-toxic. The tanned leather 
shall be substantially fat-liquored or oiled or both and the surface obtained shall be smooth and well 
set. 

3.2 Thread for Stitching 

3.2.1 Linen thread — Rot-proofed and having 5 plies shall be used for stitching. The minimum 
breaking strength of single yarn shall be 4.5 kgf (45 N) when tested according to the method given 
in IS : 1670-1970 'Method for determination of breaking load, elongation at break and tenacity of 
yarns ( first revision )\ 

3.2.2 Cotton thread — Conforming to variety No. 35 [98 tex x 8 (6 S /8)J of IS : 1720-1969 'Specification 
for cotton sewing thread ( first revision )'. 

3.3 Lining Cloth — Subject to agreement between the purchaser and the supplier, throwball covers 
may be provided with new cotton drill or canvas lining. 

4. Construction and Workmanship 

4.1 The balls shall be made from a suitable number of panels of shapes capable of giving sphericity. 

4.2 Stitching — The ball shall be stitched with linen or cotton threads and shall have 24 ± 2 stitches 
per decimetre. The stitches shall be well stretched. When the ball is fully inflated, the visible threads 
shall be not more than 2 mm deep from the surface of the ball. The panels for throwballs should 
preferably be cut with self-cutting-cum-perforating dies. 

4.3 Mouth — The mouth shall be adequate and permit the nozzle of the inflating pump or needle to 
be accommodated and suitable means provided to deflate the ball. The neck of the bladder shall be 
completely inside the mouth.

IS : 417 (Part V) - 1976 

5. Sampling and Inspection 

5.1 Sampling 

5.1.1 Lot — In any consignment, all the balls of one type manufactured from the same raw 
materials shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

5.1.2 Samples for test shall be selected at random from each lot in accordance with col 1 and 2 of 
Table 1. 

5.2 Inspection 

5.2.1 Each ball in the test samples shall first be examined for materials of construction as given 
under 3. If any ball in the test sample is noticed to have been made up of materials other than 
those specified, all the balls in the lot shall be examined and those not conforming shall be 
rejected. 

5.2.2 If the balls are made up of satisfactory materials, then each ball in the test sample shall be 
inspected for shape and dimensions (see 2), colour (see 2.3), construction and workmanship 
(see 4). 

5.2.3 During inspection of sample balls in 5.2.2 each instance of lack of conformity of the ball to 
specification shall be considered as a defect of the ball. While examining sample balls, the total 
number and types of such defects shall be noted down. 

5.3 Criterion for Acceptance 

5.3.1 A lot shall be accepted as conforming to this standard, if the corresponding test samples 
satisfy the conditions of 5.3.1.1 and 5.3.1.2. 

5.3.1.1 Total number of defects observed during testing as in 5.2.3 shall not be more than the 
corresponding acceptance number given in col 3 of Table 1. 

5.3.1.2 Total number of defects of any one type observed when tested as in 5.2.3 shall be less than 
half the corresponding acceptance number.

6. Marking — Unless otherwise required by the purchaser, each ball shall bear the 
manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark. 

6.1 ISI Certification Marking— Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

7. Packing — Each ball shall first be wrapped in polyethylene cover and than packed together 
with other balls similarly wrapped according to the instructions of the purchaser.
